31 A student connects two loudspeakers to a signal generator.
Q
signal
generator
P
As the student walks from P to Q, he notices that the loudness of the sound rises and falls
repeatedly.
What causes the loudness of the sound to vary?
A
diffraction of the sound waves
B
Doppler shift of the sound waves
C
interference of the sound waves
D
reflection of the sound waves

hints: Notice both loudspeakers are driven by the same signal generator, so they emit sound of the same frequency in phase.
Think about how the path difference from the two speakers to the ear changes as the student walks from P to Q.
Recall how superposition of two coherent waves gives loud constructive and quiet destructive regions depending on path difference.
walkthrough: Identify the set-up: two loudspeakers connected to one signal generator are two coherent sources of sound of the same frequency and constant phase difference.
As the student moves from P to Q, the distance to each speaker changes, so the path difference $\Delta x$ from the two speakers to the ear changes continuously.
By the principle of superposition, the two waves add at the ear. When they arrive in phase, where $\Delta x = n\lambda$, they interfere constructively to give a loud maximum.
When they arrive in antiphase, where $\Delta x = (n+1/2)\lambda$, they interfere destructively to give a quiet minimum.
Moving along P to Q therefore passes alternately through maxima and minima, so loudness rises and falls repeatedly. This is option C.

A.explanation: Diffraction is the spreading of sound around obstacles, but it does not produce repeated loud and quiet positions as you move from P to Q.

B.explanation: Doppler shift changes observed frequency when source or observer moves fast, but walking speed is too small and it would not cause repeated rises and falls in loudness.

C.explanation: The two speakers act as coherent sources, so their waves superpose to give constructive loud maxima and destructive quiet minima at different positions.

D.explanation: Reflection from walls could form echoes, but the regular pattern between P and Q is caused by the direct waves from the two speakers overlapping.
